author: Bhoopendra Singh Bhadauria
content: Today, I spent time understanding the fundamentals of DevOps — What it is ? Why it came into existence ? Before DevOps, software delivery involved multiple independent teams such as developers, system administrators, server administrators, testers, and operations teams. Although each team played a crucial role, the lack of coordination often resulted in delays, rework, and inefficient releases. DevOps emerged to bridge this gap. In simple terms, DevOps is a culture and process that focuses on delivering applications efficiently by emphasizing automation, continuous testing, continuous monitoring, and quality at every stage of development. What I found important is that DevOps is not limited to tools—it strongly aligns with Software Engineering principles, such as: - Streamlining the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) - Improving collaboration between teams - Building reliable and maintainable systems - Ensuring quality throughout the development process rather than at the end Understanding the reason behind DevOps makes the concepts feel more practical and purposeful. Looking forward to applying these ideas as I continue learning. hashtag #DevOps hashtag #SoftwareEngineering hashtag #SDLC hashtag #ContinuousLearning hashtag #TechSkills

author: IntelliQ IT Trainings
content: Dear hashtag #connections of IntelliQ IT Day 7| of 30days series Devops fresher must know Learning DevOps tools alone is not enough to clear interviews. Most candidates get rejected because interviews test problem-solving mindset, real-world scenarios, fundamentals and ownership, not just tools. This post explains the real reasons DevOps interviews reject candidates and what interviewers actually look for. 1: Tools ≠ DevOps “Knowing Jenkins, Docker, or Kubernetes doesn’t make you a DevOps engineer.” DevOps is about how you solve problems, not how many tools you list. Reason 2: Lack of Problem-Solving Mindset Interviewers don’t ask: “Which command?” They ask: “What will you do when production fails?” If you can’t explain your thinking, you fail. Reason 3: No Real-World Scenario Experience Candidates can explain pipelines… but struggle with scenarios like: Deployment failure Rollback strategy Monitoring & alerts This is where most rejections happen. Reason 4: Weak Fundamentals (Hidden Deal-Breaker) Many candidates jump straight to tools without understanding basics. Interviewers expect clarity on: Linux basics Networking fundamentals How applications actually run Without fundamentals, tools don’t matter. Reason 5: Poor Communication During Scenarios In real DevOps roles, how you explain your approach matters as much as the solution. Candidates often fail because they: Jump to commands without explaining Don’t communicate impact or risk Ignore rollback and stakeholder communication Interviewers want engineers who can think clearly and explain calmly under pressure.“DevOps interviews don’t reject lack of tools.
